Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a), which shows a focal opacity in the right mid-to-lower lung zone, with the follow-up image (Figure 4) reveals that the right-sided opacity has increased in density and extent, and new patchy opacities have appeared in the left lung. This pattern of progressive, multifocal airspace disease in a patient with subacute dyspnea and cough unresponsive to antibiotics is characteristic of adenocarcinoma in situ (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma), which can mimic pneumonia or organizing pneumonia but typically shows progression rather than resolution.
